Action Plan:
1. Urgent neurology referral for possible demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis); expected tests include MRI brain/spine and ophthalmic/neuro-ophthalmic assessment.  
2. Advise patient to present to Emergency Department (A&E) immediately for any progression to lower-limb weakness, new or worsening visual loss, severe headache, vomiting, or seizures.  
3. Symptomatic care: continue Ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented); avoid boxing and other upper-limb strain until specialist review; use warm baths or gentle stretching as tolerated.  
4. No disease-specific medication initiated; treatment to be guided by neurology.  
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 2-week history of numbness, tingling, and subjective weakness in left arm, most noticeable in palmar aspects of 2nd–4th fingers; worsened despite massage, warm baths, and Ibuprofen.  
• Onset/precipitating factors: Began after starting boxing classes a few weeks ago; progressively worsening.  
• Associated symptoms: Single 20-minute episode of left-eye peripheral visual field loss “a few weeks ago”; occasional fatigue-related headaches; no seizures, no lower-limb weakness.  
• Neck pain: patient said “Yes, absolutely,” then immediately “No, nothing” – conflict noted.  
• Recent illness: Severe cold/flu-like illness ~1 month ago, lasted ~2 weeks.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Medications:  
  – Ibuprofen PRN for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  – Vitamin D (dose/frequency not documented)  
  – Iron supplement (infrequent, often forgotten; dose/frequency not documented)  
  – Melatonin PRN for sleep (dose/frequency not documented)  
• Allergies: not discussed / not documented.  
• Family history: Father – hypothyroidism, unspecified autoimmune condition. Mother – type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia. No known familial neurological disorders.  
• Social: Exercises regularly; recently increased boxing activity; occasional heavy alcohol intake reported; non-smoker (not explicitly stated but implied).

Objective:
• No in-consultation physical examination; video encounter only.  
• No vitals or investigation results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left upper-limb numbness/weakness  
   – Assessment: Suspected demyelinating disease (multiple sclerosis) pending confirmation.  
   – Differential: Cervical radiculopathy, ulnar/median neuropathy, post-viral neuritis, boxing-related overuse injury.  
   – Investigations: MRI brain and cervical spine, nerve-conduction studies as indicated (via neurology).  
   – Treatment: Symptom relief with NSAIDs; suspend boxing; safety-net advice as above.  
   – Referral: Urgent neurology.

2. Transient left-eye visual field loss  
   – Assessment: Possible optic neuritis related to demyelinating process.  
   – Differential: Migraine aura, transient ischemic attack, retinal pathology.  
   – Investigations: Part of neurology work-up; may include visual evoked potentials and ophthalmology assessment.  
   – Treatment: Await specialist guidance.  
   – Referral: Included in neurology referral; ophthalmology if advised.

3. Recent viral illness (resolved)  
   – Assessment: Self-limited; no active management required.  
   – Plan: None.

• Missing/undocumented: Allergies, vital signs, formal neurological examination findings.  
• Internal conflict: Patient both affirmed and denied neck pain (“Yes, absolutely” vs “No, nothing”) – conflict noted.
